title: Restriction and composition for locally closed extension by zero
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on the small pro-étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and inverse images of ring and module sheaves [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For a locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ (a closed immersion followed by an open immersion, [def-weil-closed-immersion]), put $R_S=a^{-1}R$. For a factorization $a=v\circ c$ with $c:S\hookrightarrow V$ closed and $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ open [def-weil-open-immersion], set $a_!=v_!c_*$ on module sheaves, where $v_!$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the extension-by-zero presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] on the open slice site, equivalently the left adjoint to $v^{-1}$, and $c_*$ is direct image with its induced $R_V$-action. All coefficient rings on subschemes are inverse images of $R$. This functor is exact. Its termwise functor on unbounded derived categories is fully faithful and has a canonical natural isomorphism $a^*a_!\cong\mathrm{id}$, where $a^*$ is exact inverse image with the pulled-back coefficient ring. Restriction $a^*$ consequently induces a bijection
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(a_!M,a_!N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)
$$
for all $M,N\in D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},R_S)$.

The functor $a_!$ is independent of this factorization up to canonical isomorphisms restricting to the identity on $S$. If a factorization $a=i\circ u$ with $u$ open and $i$ closed is given, there is the same normalized identification $a_!\cong i_*u_!$. For locally closed immersions $b:T\hookrightarrow S$, there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$
\gamma_{a,b}:a_!b_!\xrightarrow{\sim}(a\circ b)_!,
$$
normalized to the identity after restriction to $T$. These identifications are unital and associative, on module sheaves and on their ordinary unbounded derived categories.

source.place: Composite consequence of proetale.tex: Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion; Tag 09BM, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact; Tag 09BN, lemma-open-immersion; Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open. Open extension is sites-modules.tex: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero; Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact. Composition of scheme immersions and its open-lifting construction are schemes.tex: Tag 02V0, lemma-composition-immersion. These passages give the open/closed factors; factorization independence and mixed composition are composite consequences, not verbatim assertions of one tag.

proof.text: Fix $a=v\circ c$, with $c:S\hookrightarrow V$ closed and $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ open. The underlying space of $X$ satisfies the minimal condition on closed subsets by the Noetherian-scheme topology theorem. This condition is inherited by the underlying spaces of all open and closed subschemes below: for an ascending chain of relative opens choose ambient open lifts and replace them by successive unions, obtaining an ascending ambient chain with the same relative intersections. Every open in such a space is quasi-compact, since an open cover with no finite subcover would recursively produce a strictly ascending chain of finite unions. Intersecting with any affine open shows that every open immersion below is quasi-compact, so all closed immersions below have the quasi-compact open complements required by the ringed open--closed theorem. For any open immersion in the argument, the closed-subset realization theorem supplies a closed subscheme supported on its closed complement; no scheme structure on that complement is presumed. Apply the ringed open--closed theorem on $X$ and $V$, always using inverse-image coefficient rings. It supplies exact $v_!,c_*$, the adjunction $v_!\dashv v^{-1}$, and isomorphisms $v^{-1}v_!\cong1$ and $c^{-1}c_*\cong1$. The module inverse images are exact by the immersion inverse-image theorem. The generic ringed-topos module-adjunction theorem, specialized to the coefficient map $c^{-1}R_V\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}R_S$, gives the closed adjunction $c^{-1}\dashv c_*$ (its tensor-formula pullback identifies with inverse image via $R_S\otimes_{R_S}M\cong M$): under the direct-image evaluation formula its Hom correspondence sends $t:c^{-1}F\to M$ to $c_*t\circ\eta_{c,F}$ and has inverse $s\mapsto\varepsilon_{c,M}\circ c^{-1}s$; the inverse-image action construction makes these maps linear over the inverse-image rings. The closed-counit theorem states explicitly that the counit of this specified module adjunction is invertible. Thus $v_!c_*$ is exact, and composing the inverse open unit with the closed counit gives a natural isomorphism $r_a:a^*a_!\xrightarrow{\sim}1$. Here $a^*\cong c^{-1}v^{-1}$ is the site-composition comparison; it is module-linear by applying the same comparison to the action maps and coefficient rings. The map $r_a$ is a restriction comparison, not the unit of a composite adjunction.

source.place: proof (2), exact locally closed extension and its restriction; Stacks Tags 09AA, 09BM, 09BN, 09AH and 03DI--03DJ

proof.text:
For an open $j$ and closed complement $i$, the localization sequence gives two useful characterizations on module sheaves: if $i^{-1}F=0$, its counit $j_!j^{-1}F\to F$ is an isomorphism; if $j^{-1}F=0$, its unit $F\to i_*i^{-1}F$ is an isomorphism. It also detects zero objects, and detects isomorphisms by applying the two exact restrictions to the kernel and cokernel. Separately, the two adjunctions of Step 1 give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(v_!c_*M,v_!c_*N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(c_*M,c_*N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,N).$$
The first bijection uses $v_!\dashv v^{-1}$ and $v^{-1}v_!\cong1$; the second uses $c^{-1}\dashv c_*$ and $c^{-1}c_*\cong1$. By the displayed adjunction formulas and their triangle identities, their composite is exactly $f\mapsto r_{a,N}\,a^*(f)\,r_{a,M}^{-1}$, and its inverse is $a_!$ on morphisms. Consequently $a_!$ is fully faithful on module sheaves. Whenever two functors in this proof are already isomorphic to the same $a_!$, there is at most one morphism between any two of their values with a specified restriction to $S$: conjugate by those isomorphisms and use this Hom bijection.

source.place: proof (2), essential images, zero detection and full faithfulness

proof.text:
We record explicitly the open restriction calculations used below. Actual module inverse image along an open is slice restriction by the ringed-open-comparison theorem. If $c:S\hookrightarrow V$ is closed and $h:W\hookrightarrow V$ open, put $S_W=S\times_VW$, with projections $c_W:S_W\to W$, $h_S:S_W\to S$. For a test object $E\to W$, both $(h^{-1}c_*M)(E)$ and $(c_{W,*}h_S^{-1}M)(E)$ are $M(S\times_VE)$, with the same restrictions and coefficient actions. Thus $h^{-1}c_*\cong c_{W,*}h_S^{-1}$. To check compatibility with the closed counit, use its inverse-image presheaf formula: a generator represented by $m\in M(S\times_VE)$ and an arrow $\phi:T\to S\times_VE$ maps to $\phi^*m\in M(T)$. When $E$ lies over $W$, this is the identical generator and restriction map for $c_W$ and $h_S^{-1}M$. The equality passes to the colimit and sheafification, proving counit compatibility. Likewise, for two opens $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ and $q:W\hookrightarrow X$, restriction of the extension presheaf for $j$ to $W$ is the extension presheaf for $U\times_XW\hookrightarrow W$: a test object over $W$ factors through $U$ exactly when it factors through their intersection; the sole summand and its section are unchanged, and otherwise both values are zero. The slice-sheafification theorem for abelian groups identifies their sheafifications. The module action is preserved because it agrees on the presheaf and module sheafification has the stated unique extension property. Hence
$$q^{-1}j_!\cong (U\times_XW\hookrightarrow W)_!\,(U\times_XW\to U)^{-1}.$$
These are open restriction calculations only; no closed-base-change theorem is assumed.

source.place: proof (2), open-slice calculations for mixed compositions; Stacks sites-modules.tex Tag 03DI and slice sheafification compatibility

proof.text: Pure open extensions compose canonically: for opens $h:W\hookrightarrow V$ and $v:V\hookrightarrow X$, $v_!h_!$ and $(vh)_!$ are both left adjoint to $h^{-1}v^{-1}\cong(vh)^{-1}$. Apply the unit-compatible-left-adjoint comparison to obtain $v_!h_!\cong(vh)_!$. All adjunctions here are open adjunctions; the comparison restricts to the identity on $W$, since its defining unit equation becomes the two open restriction identifications. Pure closed direct images compose by the evaluation formula $M(S\times_V(V\times_XE))\cong M(S\times_XE)$; the fibre-product associativity map is the identity after the canonical restriction identifications on $S$. Composition of open immersions is open from the definition, and composition of closed immersions is closed: on affine opens the two surjective ring maps compose to a surjection. These are the elementary geometric cases of Stacks Tag 02V0.

source.place: proof (2), pure open and pure closed composition; schemes.tex Tag 02V0 and proetale.tex Tags 09AA, 09BN

proof.text: Here is the shrinking argument for a closed factor. Let $c:S\hookrightarrow V$ be closed and $h:W\hookrightarrow V$ open containing the image of $S$; write $d:S\hookrightarrow W$ for its restriction. Apply the closed-subset realization theorem to $V\setminus W$, obtaining a closed immersion $e:D\hookrightarrow V$ with that image. Since $D$ is disjoint from $S$, its map to $V$ factors through the open $V\setminus S$. The cross-vanishing $(V\setminus S)^{-1}c_*=0$, followed by inverse-image composition, gives $e^{-1}c_*M=0$. The localization sequence for $h,e$ therefore identifies $h_!h^{-1}c_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}c_*M$. Step 3 identifies $h^{-1}c_*M=d_*M$. We have obtained a natural isomorphism $h_!d_*\cong c_*$ restricting to the identity on $S$: the open counit restricts to the inverse open unit by its triangle identity, and the closed restriction comparison is the counit of Step 1.

source.place: proof (2), factorization comparison by shrinking an ambient open

proof.text: For two factorizations $a=v c=v'c'$, use the open subscheme $W=V\times_XV'$ of $X$. Both maps from $S$ to $V,V'$ factor through $W$, and $d:S\hookrightarrow W$ is closed, being the restriction of $c$ (equivalently $c'$) to this open. Step 5 identifies $c_*\cong(W\hookrightarrow V)_!d_*$ and $c'_*\cong(W\hookrightarrow V')_!d_*$. Step 4 therefore identifies both extension functors with $(W\hookrightarrow X)_!d_*$. These are normalized isomorphisms: their restrictions to $S$, using $r_a$, are the identity. This proves factorization independence without a composite adjunction. Step 2 shows that the normalized comparison is unique, so comparisons via a further intersection agree and satisfy the cocycle law. The topology and scheme structure used here are literal open restrictions of the given closed immersions, not an inference that an arbitrary morphism factors through a closed subscheme merely from its image.

source.place: proof (2), independence of the closed-then-open factorization

proof.text:
We now prove the required mixed interchange. Suppose $a=i\circ u$ with $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ closed and $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ open. Because a closed immersion induces the subspace topology, choose an open $V\subset X$ with $i^{-1}V=S$; write $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ and $d:S=Z\times_XV\hookrightarrow V$. Put $A=j_!d_*M$. Open restriction and inverse-image composition give $u^{-1}i^{-1}A\cong d^{-1}j^{-1}A\cong M$. Apply the closed-subset realization theorem to $X\setminus V$ to choose a closed complement $e:D\hookrightarrow X$, and use its fibre product $B=Z\times_XD$ as a closed complement of $S$ in $Z$, with $f:B\to Z$ and $t:B\to D$. Then
$$f^{-1}i^{-1}A\cong t^{-1}e^{-1}j_!d_*M=0.$$
Write $\sigma:u^{-1}i^{-1}A\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ for the displayed restriction comparison. The localization sequence on $Z$ consequently gives a natural isomorphism $\lambda:u_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}i^{-1}A$, explicitly $\lambda=\varepsilon_{u,i^{-1}A}\circ u_!(\sigma^{-1})$, where $\varepsilon_u$ is the open counit. Transpose its inverse under the valid closed adjunction $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$ to define $\theta:A\to i_*u_!M$. The closed counit and its triangle identity identify $i^{-1}\theta$ with $\lambda^{-1}$, so it is invertible. Let $k:X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$. The restriction $k^{-1}i_*u_!M$ is zero. Step 3 gives $k^{-1}A\cong j'_!k'^{-1}d_*M$, where $k':V\setminus S\hookrightarrow V$ and $j':V\setminus S\hookrightarrow X\setminus Z$ are open; this is zero by the cross-vanishing for the closed immersion $d$. Thus both $i^{-1}\theta$ and $k^{-1}\theta$ are isomorphisms, and Step 2 detects that $\theta$ is an isomorphism. The map $\lambda$ is the open counit after $u^{-1}i^{-1}A\cong M$, so its restriction is the identity under the open unit; the same is true of $\theta$ on $S$ by the closed triangle identity. We obtain the normalized isomorphism $j_!d_*\cong i_*u_!$. This calculation supplies the previously missing mixed case, including the stated alternative-factorization identification after Step 6.

source.place: proof (2), mixed open/closed factorization; localization sequence of Stacks Tag 09AH

proof.text:
Let $a=v c:S\hookrightarrow X$ and $b=w d:T\hookrightarrow S$, with $v,w$ open and $c,d$ closed. Lift the open $W\subset S$ defining $w$ to an open $V'\subset V$ by the subspace topology for the closed immersion $c$. This gives a cartesian square $c w=h e$, with $h:V'\hookrightarrow V$ open and $e:W=S\times_VV'\hookrightarrow V'$ closed. Step 7 supplies $c_*w_!\cong h_!e_*$. Hence
$$a_!b_!=v_!c_*w_!d_*\cong v_!h_!e_*d_*\cong(vh)_!(ed)_*.$$
Here $vh$ is open and $ed$ is closed by Step 4, so the last functor is extension by zero for the exhibited factorization of $ab$. Compare it to the chosen $(ab)_!$ using Step 6; the result is $\gamma_{a,b}$. Every map in the construction restricts to the identity on $T$, proving its normalization. In particular $a_!b_!$ lies in the same essential image as $(ab)_!$.

source.place: proof (2), compatibility with arbitrary mixed compositions; schemes.tex Tag 02V0 open-lifting argument

proof.text: The comparisons are independent of every choice and satisfy the claimed laws by the Hom uniqueness in Step 2, rather than uniqueness of nonexistent composite adjoints. Indeed, after the isomorphisms of Steps 6 and 8, the source and target of two candidate comparisons both lie in the essential image of the same locally closed extension functor. Their restrictions agree (they are the identity), so the comparisons agree. For an identity immersion the identity comparison has that normalization; this proves both unit laws. For three composable immersions $a,b,d$, both maps from $a_!b_!d_!M$ to $(abd)_!M$ lie between objects in the essential image of $(abd)_!$: apply Step 8 twice, in either order. After restriction to the final source they are both the identity, by the normalized restriction comparisons and inverse-image associativity. Step 2 makes them equal. The inverse-image associativity here is the canonical site-composition associativity: the two fibre-product comparisons agree by the universal property, and their adjoint inverse-image comparisons agree by the unit normalization. This proves associativity, including mixed cases, on module sheaves.

source.place: proof (2), unit and associativity laws for normalized composition

proof.text:
Finally pass all these constructions to the ordinary unbounded derived categories. The exact-functor derived-factorization theorem applies to each open extension, closed direct image and immersion inverse image, so their induced functors are represented termwise with no boundedness or resolution assumption. The termwise-adjunction theorem supplies the open and closed units, counits and triangle identities on complexes separately. Apply the localization universal property to those natural transformations: it descends units and counits to the derived functors, and its equality-detection clause descends both triangle identities. We therefore have $D(v_!)\dashv D(v^{-1})$ and $D(c^{-1})\dashv D(c_*)$, still with invertible open unit and closed counit. The two successive Hom transpositions of Step 2 now give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X,R)}(a_!M,a_!N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S,R_S)}(M,N),\qquad f\longmapsto r_{a,N}\,a^*(f)\,r_{a,M}^{-1}.$$
Thus the termwise locally closed extension is fully faithful and restriction gives exactly the stated Hom bijection. The same localization statement descends $r_a$, the factorization and mixed comparisons, and $\gamma$. Their normalization, unit and associativity identities already hold as natural transformations of complexes (degreewise the module identities above), so equality detection proves them on the entire unbounded derived categories. No assertion that $a_!\dashv a^*$ is used.

split_report.summary: Repair of E3/C4/F2: removed the false adjunction v_!c_* ⊣ c^{-1}v^{-1} and rebuilt every dependent step. Exactness and the restriction comparison use the two valid factor adjunctions; their separate Hom transpositions give full faithfulness. Localization and explicit open-slice calculations prove shrinking and the mixed open/closed interchange, which give factorization independence and composition. Faithfulness of restriction proves coherence. Exact termwise localization descends the two factor adjunctions and all comparisons to unbounded derived categories. No statement change or new node. tool_uses.why: Arbitrary-ring pro-etale localization, exactness, open adjunction, closed counit and zero detection; these implement locally closed extension rather than a coefficient-comparison theorem.
Exact module inverse image for pulled-back ring sheaves, needed for the two exact factor adjunctions and termwise derived functors.
Canonical composition of inverse images and direct images; gives coherent comparison of coefficient rings and restrictions.
Identifies actual arbitrary-ring open inverse image with slice evaluation, used to verify the closed-direct-image and open-extension restriction calculations.
Generic slice sheafification compatibility for abelian presheaves, used before uniquely transporting the arbitrary-ring module actions.
Unit-compatible uniqueness is applied solely to the genuine open-extension adjunctions in pure open composition.
Generic termwise descent of exact functors to ordinary unbounded derived categories without resolutions.
Supplies termwise units/counits and triangles for the separate open and closed adjunctions on complexes.
Generic descent and equality detection for natural transformations; descends the separate adjunctions and all coherence maps.
Generic minimal condition on the underlying closed subsets of the given Noetherian scheme; a short subspace/open-cover argument checks every quasi-compactness hypothesis of localization.
Generic arbitrary-ring module inverse-image/direct-image adjunction, specialized to the identity coefficient map; supplies the valid closed adjunction in the required direction.
Specifies that the actual counit of the arbitrary-ring closed module adjunction is invertible, fixing the normalization of restriction rather than using an unspecified isomorphism.
